title: Being noted for his mute at the Embers; two years in and out
summary: By the Embers years he was established for his mute and liked its crisp, stinging sound, working there off and on for about two years.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Well when you went into the Embers, then, were you playing open horn?

No I had my mutes (Inaudible) because I was -- this is after -- well, this is much after Fats. I mean I had been established, because I'm noted for my mute, you know? And I like it. I like the mute. I like the -- I like that crisp and stinging sound, you know, effect that the mute can give with me a mute.
How long did your going in and out of the Embers go on, Herman? Were you part of a regular circuit there?
I would say about -- two years, maybe, three years?
Yeah, two, and two anyway, I would say.
